clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within the next year: June grew homesick and wrote to her sister daily; Walter stayed out in the orchard from dark to dark; Glen fought at his new school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees; June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The shifts pile up through the first year in the valley, with Walter and Glen showing trouble at work and school, June anxious and then withdrawn, and Walter and June in conflict, until June's move toward the choir in September marks the beginning of settling.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 and its sale in October: Walter drank heavily; Walter and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April; Ida was told to stop work for her heart trouble in May; Walter stopped drinking and took pruning work in October. The shifts move through the family as the loss of the orchard unsettled Walter, Glen stepped in to manage, and the children showed trouble, until Walter's shift toward work in October marks settling.

clusters.name: Glen lost his job at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975, within the next year: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck for hours; Glen and Marian fought loud at night over money; Glen and Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and distanced from Marian; Walter drank again after six years sober; Nora ate again and made the track team in June. The shifts touch Nora most closely—her weight loss and withdrawal—while Glen and Marian clash and turn to work, and Walter's drinking marks the wider strain; Nora's return to eating in June shows settling.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, within the next year and a half: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and distanced from the kitchen rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis rowed most nights; Wilma moved to a flat in town in June 1991; Nora's eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts show Nora caught between Wilma and Hollis, with Owen and Lily troubled in the household, Nora's eczema marking her strain, until Wilma's move to town in June and the eczema's clearing mark settling.

periods.name: the year Dad lost his job
periods.words: The one that stands out is the year Dad lost his job, when I was 14.

A few days around a real threat with the family as it was before once it is over is an acute episode, not a period.

1996–1997: not enough in the diagram to choose a reading. One more shift that counts is Nora's anxiety up in November 1996, but the only change in the family among these events is marked neverOpens—Marian's overfunctioning in January 1997 has no date anyone is sure of. Without a change in who is in the family or in how a key member functions on a known date, there is not enough to open a period.
